title: Depth of a finite module
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I\subset R$ an ideal and $M$ a finite (finitely generated) $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]; write $IM\subset M$ for the submodule generated by the products $am$ with $a\in I$, $m\in M$. The *$I$-depth* $\operatorname{depth}_I(M)\in\{0,1,2,\dots\}\cup\{\infty\}$ is defined as follows: (1) if $IM\neq M$, it is the supremum in $\{0,1,2,\dots\}\cup\{\infty\}$ of the lengths $r$ of the $M$-regular sequences $f_1,\dots,f_r$ in $I$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] (the empty sequence, $r=0$, is one, since $M/0\cdot M=M\neq0$); (2) if $IM=M$ (for instance $M=0$, or $I=R$), $\operatorname{depth}_I(M)=\infty$. If $(R,\mathfrak m)$ is a local ring (a commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$), $\operatorname{depth}(M):=\operatorname{depth}_{\mathfrak m}(M)$ is the *depth* of $M$, and the depth of the local ring $R$ is $\operatorname{depth}(R)$, the depth of $R$ as a module over itself.

mathlib_candidate.how: NOT in the Mathlib pinned by the source repository (rev 0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474: Mathlib/RingTheory/Depth/ has only Rees.lean, and Regular/Depth.lean is a 10-line deprecated_module stub); found by loogle in upstream Mathlib and read in the upstream master file (raw.githubusercontent.com, mathlib4 master, fetched 2026-10-10; sed -n 60,80p, 100,116p, 310,380p): line 66 `ModuleCat.depth N M : ℕ∞ := sSup {n : ℕ∞ | ∀ i : ℕ, i < n → Subsingleton (Ext N M i)}`, line 73 `Ideal.depth I M := ModuleCat.depth (Shrink (R ⧸ I)) M` (tagged @[stacks 00LI], with the remark that it coincides with the regular-sequence definition when R is Noetherian and IM ≠ M), line 78 `IsLocalRing.depth M := (maximalIdeal R).depth M`. Different convention: depth is defined by vanishing of Ext^i(R/I, M), for M : ModuleCat R, with no finiteness hypothesis. Agreement with this node is a theorem: for M = 0 both are ∞ (Ideal.depth_eq_top_of_subsingleton, line 110); for R Noetherian, M finite and IM ≠ M, Ideal.depth_eq_sSup_length_isRegular (line 337; ModuleCat version line 316, local case IsLocalRing.depth_eq_sSup_length_isRegular line 369, needing M nontrivial) gives the supremum of lengths of M-regular sequences in I, by the Rees theorem of Depth/Rees.lean; for R not Noetherian, or IM = M with M ≠ 0, the two need not agree without a proof (Stacks' value is ∞ by fiat). Hence not a leaf (B8).

split_report.summary: Checked against Stacks 00LI (algebra.tex line 17766) and 00LF (line 16594): the definition agrees clause by clause (finite module, IM ≠ M: supremum in {0,1,...,∞} of lengths of M-regular sequences in I; IM = M: ∞; local case depth_m). def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence matches 00LF including condition (2) M/(f_1..f_r)M ≠ 0. Made the statement self-contained: cited def-weil-finitely-generated-module for 'finite module', defined IM and 'local ring' inline, said why the empty sequence counts (M ≠ 0 when IM ≠ M), and that depth(R) is the depth of R as a module over itself. The six citers use the definition only as stated (depth ≥ d from an R-regular sequence of length d in m with mR ≠ R; depth(M) = d for maximal Cohen–Macaulay). Mathlib: the pinned Mathlib has no depth (Regular/Depth.lean is a deprecation stub, Depth/Rees.lean only the Rees theorem); upstream Mathlib's Ideal.depth / IsLocalRing.depth are Ext-based, recorded as mathlib_candidate; status left unsplit (B8).
